#### **VIKTOR**

## [The one hire every department wants a piece of](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main12-hl)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/3c1e3f4c-69ba-4dd3-bbb0-da2731c0ce1d/aivalley_main12_1280x720__1_.jpg?t=1793022354)
Caption: [Courtesy: Viktor](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main12-hl)

My name is Viktor. I'm the AI employee your whole company shares, and 70,000+ teams have hired me.

Finance asks for last month's revenue by plan, pulled from Stripe and matched against the books. Sales asks me to clean up stale deals in HubSpot and nudge each owner. Marketing wants to know which Google Ads campaigns burned budget last week. Engineering hands me a pull request to review. Ops asks for a way to track vendor contracts and gets a web app at a live link.

Each team teaches me how it works, and I remember. I work inside the 3,200+ tools you connect and hand back the finished thing. Anything I can't undo waits for a person to approve it. SOC 2 certified.

Give me one request from every team this week. 

[Start free, no credit card, up to $100 in credits.](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main12)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

**3/ **[**Anthropic is going public, and it could be the biggest IPO ever.**](https://www.anthropic.com/news/s1-sec) The Claude maker has officially filed for its IPO under the ticker ANT, potentially listing on November 9th. There's talk of raising $100B at a whopping $2T valuation, which would beat SpaceX's recent $86B IPO record. Anthropic hasn't confirmed either number. (Not bad for a company founded five years ago)

Its financials are even wilder. It made $16.3B in the first half of 2026, up from $1.2B a year earlier, or roughly $6.6M in revenue per employee. It also reported an $80.7B net loss, although $72.4B of that was largely noncash accounting charges tied to its rising valuation. The operating loss was closer to $693M.

What I'm curious about is how public investors will price a company growing this quickly while committing hundreds of billions to compute. At a $1.5T valuation, they're paying roughly 46 times annualized first-half revenue. That's a pretty enormous bet that AI demand, and Anthropic's share of it, will keep growing for years.

And with OpenAI still private, Anthropic could become Wall Street's first proper test of what a frontier AI lab is actually worth.

Youtube: Meet Kimi K3.1 Pro (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DIyHTpfWctU)

**3/ **[**Kimi K3.1 Pro is giving the big AI labs something to worry about.**](https://www.kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro) Moonshot's new 2.8T-parameter model ranks fourth on Artificial Analysis, ahead of GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Fable 5.1, and competes with Opus 5.5 on several benchmarks. Pretty remarkable for a Chinese model whose weights are expected on November 4.

[One example](https://x.com/atomic_chat_hq/status/2113700709506113948?s=20) caught my attention: teams of five Kimi and Opus 5.5 agents were given the same video-making task. Kimi finished in 26 minutes for $7.31. Opus took two hours and cost $76.42. That's roughly 10x cheaper and nearly 5x faster on that particular task. I'd like to see how consistently it performs across other projects, but those numbers are hard to ignore.

API pricing starts at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens, although Kimi reportedly consumes more tokens than some rivals. There's also a Highspeed version that's 2–3x faster.

The bigger story might be what happens when the weights drop. If a model this competitive can be downloaded and run independently, proprietary labs have another reason to justify their premium pricing. Being slightly better on benchmarks won't be enough for every customer.

DOTS: A GUIDE FOR PUTTING OPENAI’S ALWAYS-ON AGENTS TO WORK https://every.?ev_audience=free


HOW EVERY’S TEAM USES DOTS TO CATCH MISTAKES, ANSWER EMAIL, BOOK APPOINTMENTS, AND RUN TASKS FROM SLACK https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Laura Entis https://every.?ev_audience=free and Opus 5.5 https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

This is a free preview of a subscribers-only post.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



You promised someone feedback in Slack, agreed to a deadline in a meeting, and have a handful of scheduling requests buried in your inbox. Keeping track of all those commitments is a job in itself.

That’s where Dots comes in. A proactive, always-on personal agent OpenAI built into ChatGPT, your Dot can monitor your Slack, email, calendar and the other places you work to catch errors and bring you reminders. It can also complete tasks for you, like answering emails, booking a doctor’s appointment, or making edits to a draft.

Our guide walks you through how to set up your Dot and includes seven workflows the Every team uses, each with a prompt you can copy.

Inside, you’ll learn how to:

 * Build a running list of commitments. Have your Dot review Slack and email for unanswered requests, deadlines, and decisions. Ask for a link to each original message, why it needs your attention, and a suggested next step.
 * Catch inconsistencies across apps. Our team’s Dots have flagged an outdated article summary and launch emails referencing a feature that hadn’t shipped yet. The guide includes a prompt for checking your work for similar discrepancies.
 * Set rules for inbox triage and scheduling. Ask your Dot to draft replies, check shared calendars, and protect your writing time. Include an explicit boundary: “Don’t send anything without my approval, and save any corrections I give you for next time.”
 * Run multistep projects from Slack. Specify the app, computer, action, and destination, then ask your Dot to report back with a result link and anything requiring your help.

Dots currently requires ChatGPT Business Premium. It’s especially useful for people juggling teams, clients, or projects; focused, linear work may offer fewer reasons to use it.

Full-duplex voice models listen and speak at the same time, but only if they’re trained on data that sounds like real conversation. Open-source and synthetic datasets rarely do. Join Voices and AlphaSignal on Tuesday, October 27 at 1 PM ET as Sully Goolamnobee, Product Manager, AI Voice, covers the three requirements for full-duplex training data and how custom conversational datasets are built to meet them. Live Q&A included.

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

**1/ **[**Microsoft thinks it's getting close to medical superintelligence**](https://microsoft.ai/news/building-medical-superintelligence/)**.** Its AI diagnostic system, MAI-DxO, solved 83% of complex medical cases, compared with 36% for generalist doctors, according to a [Science study](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aeh7930). Impressive, although these were simulated cases, and you'd probably have specialists handling cases this difficult in a real hospital.

The numbers get more interesting when you look at the underlying models. GPT-5 already scored 79% without Microsoft's multi-agent setup, which added just four points. GPT-5.5 improved more, from 72% to nearly 87%. Makes me wonder how much of the breakthrough is clever orchestration versus simply having better models.

Mustafa Suleyman is now talking about AI predicting patients' future health from medical records as early as 2027. If that works reliably, catching diseases before symptoms appear could be a much bigger deal than winning diagnostic benchmarks.

**2/ ****[AI found a 14-year-old PHP bug. Hackers got there before the patch.](https://openai.com/index/coordinated-disclosure-of-critical-vulnerabilities/)** Two critical vulnerabilities, called _php2shell_, allow attackers to execute code on vulnerable servers without logging in. Palo Alto Networks identified 22.6 million potentially vulnerable instances, and Cloudflare reportedly saw millions of exploitation attempts within hours of the news leaking.

The bugs had been sitting in PHP for roughly 14 years. A weaker version even surfaced in 2024 without much concern. OpenAI says GPT-5.6 Sol helped turn that suspicious behavior into a working exploit.

I suspect we'll see plenty more of this. There's decades of old code nobody has properly examined, and AI is getting pretty good at finding things humans missed. OpenAI has announced [$1B for Patch the Planet](https://gizmodo.com/openai-wants-to-patch-the-planet-with-its-own-ai-2000829119) to help organizations audit their systems, but finding bugs faster doesn't mean they'll get fixed faster. Getting millions of servers updated is still a painfully human problem.

[PHP has released fixes](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php). No complete workaround, so update if you're running it.
